plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked thermometer chart from Eunice Foote's November 1856 paper compares dry air (96 °F / 35.6 °C) vs damp air (108 °F / 42.2 °C), and ambient air (106 °F / 41.1 °C) vs carbonic acid gas / CO₂ (125 °F / 51.7 °C, +19 °F hotter) in sunlit 30-inch glass cylinders.

teach_overlay.scale: inside a 30-inch glass tube in the New York sun, carbon dioxide climbed 19 degrees Fahrenheit hotter than ordinary air — the first experimental clue to how changing air changes Earth's climate
